guidance: Evaluation only: this page models the expression language, not your repository. Supply the contexts you want it to read, check the value and type it reports, and remember that an if: without a status function also needs the job to be succeeding, which GitHub applies as an implicit success().
method: Parses and evaluates one expression from a workflow if:, env: or runs-on: against a JSON document of contexts. The outer ${{ }} wrapper is optional and stripped. Literals are true, false, null, numbers in any form the JSON grammar accepts plus hexadecimal (0xff), signs and exponents, and single-quoted strings where '' stands for a literal quote; double-quoted strings are refused because the language rejects them. The operator table is the documented one, from tightest to loosest binding: grouping, index, property dereference, !, the relational operators < <= > >=, then == and !=, then && and ||, all left-associative. There are no arithmetic operators, so + - * / and % are refused rather than guessed at. ! always yields a boolean, while && and || short-circuit and return one of their operands, so an expression can evaluate to a string or a number. Equality is loose: when the kinds differ both sides are coerced to a number, where null is 0, true is 1, false is 0, a string is read as a number (the empty string is 0, anything unparseable is NaN) and an array or object is NaN; NaN never equals anything, and arrays and objects are equal only when they are the same value. Strings compare ignoring case, ordinal rather than by locale, and the same case folding applies to < <= > >= once both sides are strings; otherwise relational comparisons coerce to numbers and are false when either side is NaN, so true > false is true and '10' < '9' is true while 10 > '9' is true. Property dereference and index access are case-insensitive for names, a property the object does not have is null, an index outside an array is null, an index on a string or number is null, and * collects the values of an object or the items of an array into an array that later dereferences map over, which is how github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name returns the label names. The functions are contains (substring or array membership, case-insensitive), startsWith and endsWith, format with {N} placeholders and {{ }} escapes, join with a comma default, toJSON with two-space indentation, fromJSON, and case(predicate, value, ..., default) whose predicates must be booleans rather than merely truthy. success(), failure(), cancelled() and always() read the earlier-steps setting on the form. An if: condition runs when the value is truthy and, unless the expression calls one of those four status functions, when earlier steps have succeeded, which is the implicit success() GitHub applies; the plain-value mode reports truthiness alone. hashFiles() needs the workflow workspace and is refused, secrets is never available inside an expression, expressions are limited to 2,000 characters and the contexts JSON to 20,000, and nesting is capped at 60 levels. Everything runs in the browser with the browser's own JSON parser: nothing is stored, uploaded or fetched.
